name: Shiftie
summary: Rota building, clock-ins, leave and shift swaps for shift-based businesses. Not an HR or payroll platform, so those stay separate purchases.
best_for: shift-based businesses (hospitality, retail, leisure) that want quick rota building, clock-ins and leave management without spreadsheet pain
skip_if: you need full HR, payroll and performance management in one system, or your team doesn't work in shifts at all
honest_knock: It's focused, affordable rota software, which means it does scheduling, clock-ins, leave and swaps well, but it isn't a full HR or payroll platform, so a growing business will still bolt on payroll and HR tools around it. Pricing is low, but the per-active-employee model means a large seasonal team in a busy month costs more than the headline suggests. For shift-based scheduling specifically, it's a clean, cheap fit.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month per active employee for the first 30, then £1.50 per employee above 30
pricing.notes: (price re-verified 24 September 2026, unchanged since 5 September) £2.75 per active employee per month for the first 30, then £1.50 for each employee above 30 — the reduced rate is marginal, not retroactive. Measured on the vendor's own pricing slider: 1 employee £2.75, 5 £13.75, 10 £27.50, 15 £41.25, 30 £82.50, 31 £84.00, 50 £112.50, 100 £187.50, 150 £262.50, 199 £336.00. At 200 employees the slider stops quoting and switches to Custom Pricing. There is no minimum and no entry-plan floor: one employee costs £2.75. Monthly billing only — no annual option is offered anywhere on the page. Billing is in arrears: at the start of each month you are charged for users marked active during the previous month. 28-day free trial, no card details required, and 7-day UK-based support included. Cancelling is a button in the billing section; access runs to the end of the current billing period, and the cancellation can be reversed until then. Note the domain move: shiftie.co.uk now redirects to shiftie.co.

compare_with.why: comparable scheduling platforms: Shiftie tends to undercut on price; compare on payroll/HR features you actually need

claims.claim: Each week I rebuild the rota in a spreadsheet, and leave requests and shift swaps get lost along the way.
claims.observed: Half of this pain was tried. Five test employees without an e-mail address and a week rota of 25 shifts were made in 5 min 31 s, from the first employee at 19:06:16 to the rota at 19:11:47, including two redos caused by the time picker. Leave requests and shift swaps were not tried.
claims.plan: Trial account; 5 test employees and a week rota of 25 shifts were built; publishing was not confirmed; the plans were read on the public pricing page; nothing was bought
claims.comparability: The pain of the audience group against a test that only built a rota; swaps and leave were not tried.
claims.buying_consequence: Building a week rota in the app went fast; whether leave requests and shift swaps stop getting lost is open.

claims.observed: After the employees were added to the schedule and Repeat shift was used, the rota showed Other Employees 25 Shifts - 200h 0m for the week, with the button Publish 25 Shifts and costs of £ 0,00 because no pay rate was set.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session built a week rota in a Shiftie trial. Five test employees were added without an e-mail address and 25 shifts (200h 0m) for the week 23 Nov to 29 Nov were made with Repeat shift. From the first employee at 19:06:16 to the finished rota at 19:11:47 took 5 min 31 s, including two redos because the time picker swallowed a click or read a typed time wrongly. The employees only entered the rota after Add Employee on the Schedule page. Publishing was not confirmed: the publish window says nothing about e-mail or text messages, and the Notifications page lists Shift Reminders by text message, whose switch was not read. The trial lasts 28 days and no card was asked; the pricing page shows £2.75 per employee a month for the first 30, £1.50 for each above that, and an Enterprise route for more than 200 employees. The button Add Payment Method was not clicked, so no checkout was seen. Swaps, leave and cancelling were not tried. Account and start: we created the account (a trial with 28 days left) and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser on 18 Nov 2026. The dossier name is Shiftie and the review is on OSM (osm/shiftie-review.html). The marketing site is shiftie.co and the app runs on shiftie.app; shiftie.co links to it. The interface language was already English (UK) with a 24 hour clock. The cookie banner was answered with Reject and the setup checklist (0 / 7) was folded away. Audience: the group Pubs, shops and venues running shift rotas; the pain is that each week the rota is rebuilt in a spreadsheet and that leave requests and shift swaps get lost. The second dossier group, employers that run payroll on separate software, was not tested. Core action: from Team, Add, Add New Employee, five test employees were created. The form requires First Name, Last Name, Permissions (Employee) and Default Job Role (only Management existed); the invite e-mail field was left empty, so the employees show as No Email and nobody was invited. The employees did not appear in the rota by themselves: on the Schedule page Add Employee, ADD EMPLOYEES TO Default Schedule, five ticks and Assign 5 Employees was needed. For the week Mon 23 Nov to Sun 29 Nov a shift was created per person from a cell with Shift time and End time, Repeat shift switched on and the days chosen, then Create 5 Shifts: 09:00 to 17:00 Monday to Friday, 12:00 to 20:00 Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 15:00 Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 18:00 Monday to Friday, and 14:00 to 22:00 Wednesday to Sunday. The result was Other Employees 25 Shifts - 200h 0m with the button Publish 25 Shifts and costs of £ 0,00 because no pay rate was set. Time: the first employee was added at 19:06:16 and the rota with 25 shifts stood at 19:11:47, so 5 min 31 s for creating 5 employees and 5 shifts per person with Repeat shift. That includes two redos: the time picker sometimes swallowed a click or read a typed 0700 as 01:00 or 02:00, so two employees had to be redone. The order that worked: click the field, type the hour (it jumps to the minutes), type 00, click outside the field, then continue. Seen but not investigated: two of the test employees show a break of 3m on Thursday next to the coffee cup, which the tester did not set; the screenshots show 0m, and the cause was not looked into; it is noted only as observed behaviour. Publishing: not confirmed. The button Publish 25 Shifts opens PUBLISH SHIFTS FOR Mon 23 Nov - Sun 29 Nov with Employees (All Employees, All Open Shifts), Groups, Job Roles and Tags and a second button Publish 25 Shifts; the window says nothing about e-mail or text messages. Settings, Notifications shows Manage SMS Notifications and Shift Reminders: Send employees notifications before their shifts' start times.; the position of that switch was not read. Because the app does not say that nothing is sent, the tester did not publish. The employees have no e-mail address. Plans up to the payment: Read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026. Public pricing page (shiftie.co/pricing/): the Monthly Plan shows £2.75 per month at 1 employee (Employees First 1 x £2.75 = £2.75) and, with the slider at 30, First 30 x £2.75 = £82.50. The FAQ says: For up to 30 employees, Shiftie is £2.75 per employee. Beyond 30, additional employees are £1.50 each (the text is cut off on the page). Enterprise is shown for more than 200 employees, with the buttons LET'S CHAT and BOOK A DEMO, which were not used. The page says All plans come with a free 28-day trial and No card details required. Inside the app (Settings, Billing Details): only the lines Payment Method and You don't have any payment methods on file. and the button Add Payment Method; no plans or prices are shown in the app. The button was not clicked, so no card field, tax amount or total was seen. This matches the dossier (pricing rule and price check of 24 Sep 2026). Prices were not changed by this delivery. Trial: 28 days, no card requested so far; no limit on the number of employees was seen (5 were created without a message). Cancelling: not tested. Not tested: publishing, swapping shifts, leave requests, inviting employees, time clock and timesheets, the payroll link, cancelling, the phone app and the second dossier group. Clean up (still so): the account, the 5 test employees and the 25 unpublished shifts for the week 23 to 29 Nov stay in the trial account; nobody was invited and nothing was published; the own tab was closed. The Billing Details screen was not used as a screenshot because it shows a company address.
exit_test.awkward: The time picker sometimes swallowed a click or read a typed 0700 as 01:00 or 02:00, so two employees had to be redone. Employees did not appear in the rota until they were added on the Schedule page. The publish window does not say whether employees get an e-mail or a text, while Settings lists text reminders for shifts, so it stays unclear what a first publish would send. Two of the test employees showed a break of 3m on Thursday that the tester did not set, which was not investigated.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Publishing the rota, so what employees actually get by e-mail or text.
Swapping shifts and leave requests.
Inviting employees, the time clock and timesheets, and the payroll link.
The phone app.
A card field, a tax amount and a total.
Cancelling; there was no subscription.
Moving logged hours into a separate payroll tool, the need of our second audience.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 18 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 19:06 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session built a week rota in a Shiftie trial. Five test employees were added without an e-mail address and 25 shifts (200h 0m) for the week 23 Nov to 29 Nov were made with Repeat shift. From the first employee at 19:06:16 to the finished rota at 19:11:47 took 5 min 31 s, including two redos because the time picker swallowed a click or read a typed time wrongly. The employees only entered the rota after Add Employee on the Schedule page. Publishing was not confirmed: the publish window says nothing about e-mail or text messages, and the Notifications page lists Shift Reminders by text message, whose switch was not read. The trial lasts 28 days and no card was asked; the pricing page shows £2.75 per employee a month for the first 30, £1.50 for each above that, and an Enterprise route for more than 200 employees. The button Add Payment Method was not clicked, so no checkout was seen. Swaps, leave and cancelling were not tried. Account and start: we created the account (a trial with 28 days left) and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser on 18 Nov 2026. The dossier name is Shiftie and the review is on OSM (osm/shiftie-review.html). The marketing site is shiftie.co and the app runs on shiftie.app; shiftie.co links to it. The interface language was already English (UK) with a 24 hour clock. The cookie banner was answered with Reject and the setup checklist (0 / 7) was folded away. Audience: the group Pubs, shops and venues running shift rotas; the pain is that each week the rota is rebuilt in a spreadsheet and that leave requests and shift swaps get lost. The second dossier group, employers that run payroll on separate software, was not tested. Core action: from Team, Add, Add New Employee, five test employees were created. The form requires First Name, Last Name, Permissions (Employee) and Default Job Role (only Management existed); the invite e-mail field was left empty, so the employees show as No Email and nobody was invited. The employees did not appear in the rota by themselves: on the Schedule page Add Employee, ADD EMPLOYEES TO Default Schedule, five ticks and Assign 5 Employees was needed. For the week Mon 23 Nov to Sun 29 Nov a shift was created per person from a cell with Shift time and End time, Repeat shift switched on and the days chosen, then Create 5 Shifts: 09:00 to 17:00 Monday to Friday, 12:00 to 20:00 Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 15:00 Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 18:00 Monday to Friday, and 14:00 to 22:00 Wednesday to Sunday. The result was Other Employees 25 Shifts - 200h 0m with the button Publish 25 Shifts and costs of £ 0,00 because no pay rate was set. Time: the first employee was added at 19:06:16 and the rota with 25 shifts stood at 19:11:47, so 5 min 31 s for creating 5 employees and 5 shifts per person with Repeat shift. That includes two redos: the time picker sometimes swallowed a click or read a typed 0700 as 01:00 or 02:00, so two employees had to be redone. The order that worked: click the field, type the hour (it jumps to the minutes), type 00, click outside the field, then continue. Seen but not investigated: two of the test employees show a break of 3m on Thursday next to the coffee cup, which the tester did not set; the screenshots show 0m, and the cause was not looked into; it is noted only as observed behaviour. Publishing: not confirmed. The button Publish 25 Shifts opens PUBLISH SHIFTS FOR Mon 23 Nov - Sun 29 Nov with Employees (All Employees, All Open Shifts), Groups, Job Roles and Tags and a second button Publish 25 Shifts; the window says nothing about e-mail or text messages. Settings, Notifications shows Manage SMS Notifications and Shift Reminders: Send employees notifications before their shifts' start times.; the position of that switch was not read. Because the app does not say that nothing is sent, the tester did not publish. The employees have no e-mail address. Plans up to the payment: Read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026. Public pricing page (shiftie.co/pricing/): the Monthly Plan shows £2.75 per month at 1 employee (Employees First 1 x £2.75 = £2.75) and, with the slider at 30, First 30 x £2.75 = £82.50. The FAQ says: For up to 30 employees, Shiftie is £2.75 per employee. Beyond 30, additional employees are £1.50 each (the text is cut off on the page). Enterprise is shown for more than 200 employees, with the buttons LET'S CHAT and BOOK A DEMO, which were not used. The page says All plans come with a free 28-day trial and No card details required. Inside the app (Settings, Billing Details): only the lines Payment Method and You don't have any payment methods on file. and the button Add Payment Method; no plans or prices are shown in the app. The button was not clicked, so no card field, tax amount or total was seen. This matches the dossier (pricing rule and price check of 24 Sep 2026). Prices were not changed by this delivery. Trial: 28 days, no card requested so far; no limit on the number of employees was seen (5 were created without a message). Cancelling: not tested. Not tested: publishing, swapping shifts, leave requests, inviting employees, time clock and timesheets, the payroll link, cancelling, the phone app and the second dossier group. Clean up (still so): the account, the 5 test employees and the 25 unpublished shifts for the week 23 to 29 Nov stay in the trial account; nobody was invited and nothing was published; the own tab was closed. The Billing Details screen was not used as a screenshot because it shows a company address.
exit_test.awkward: The time picker sometimes swallowed a click or read a typed 0700 as 01:00 or 02:00, so two employees had to be redone. Employees did not appear in the rota until they were added on the Schedule page. The publish window does not say whether employees get an e-mail or a text, while Settings lists text reminders for shifts, so it stays unclear what a first publish would send. Two of the test employees showed a break of 3m on Thursday that the tester did not set, which was not investigated.
